fix(cache): do not cache credential-bearing same-origin redirects under the alias key

When the cache interceptor is the outermost layer and the redirect
interceptor is inside it, the cache key and handler are built from the
original request. The redirect handler suppresses the intermediate
redirect response, so the cache handler only ever receives the final

entry on origin, method, path and Vary only — never the credential. So a
later request to the alias URL by a different principal, or by an

🐞 fix: prevent stale _setValid() calls from overwriting isValid/isValidating (#13599)

* fix: prevent a stale _setValid() call from overwriting a newer isValid result

_setValid() is fired-and-forget from 9 call sites and never awaited by its
caller, with no guard against out-of-order completion. If an earlier call
is still awaiting async validation when a later one starts and finishes
first, the earlier one can still commit its now-stale isValid result
afterward, silently overwriting the correct, current one.

Give each call a monotonic id and skip the commit if a newer call has
started since, mirroring the staleness check onChange already does
per-field via _updateIsFieldValueUpdated.

* fix: also guard the isValidating commit inside _setValid's resolver branch

Found while reviewing the isValid fix: _updateIsValidating() has the exact
same staleness exposure. It unconditionally clears validatingFields and
reports isValidating: false, so a superseded _setValid() call finishing
after

🐞 fix(reset): update isValid when reset drops a pending validation (#13994)

Since #13908, reset() advances the _setValid call id so an isValid pass
still in flight is dropped: it validated the values from before the
reset. Nothing then validates the reset values. reset() does not start a
pass, and with non-empty values it marks the form mounted, so useForm's
effect skips one too. A field that re-renders re-registers and starts a
pass, which hides this; a memoised field does not, and isValid stays
false for a valid record until a field changes.

Keep the reset check inside _setValid instead: a pass that settles after
a reset, with no newer pass started, runs again for the current values.
keepIsValid still returns before any pass runs.

Fixes #13993

perf: keep zod out of the browser (#18576)

> Written by AI (Claude Code). The measurements were also run by AI.

## What

The `json` validator checks values against a field's `jsonSchema` with
zod. The admin's login and account forms import validators like `email`
and `password` from `payload/shared`, which brings in the whole
validations module, including its `await import('zod')`. Bundlers
compile every `import()` target, so every app compiled all of zod for
the browser. But `jsonSchema` is a server-only field property: Payload
removes it from the client config, so this check never runs in the
browser.

The JSON Schema check moves into `#validateJSONSchema`. That's a
package-private import defined in the `imports` field of `package.json`:
browsers get a version that does nothing, and everything else gets the
zod version. `json()` behaves exactly as before on the server, including
when your own code calls it.

`imports` works like `exports`, but for paths a package only uses
internal

refactor(ui): normalize form state before request serialization (#18801)

Requires [#18793](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/18793)

Removes the TanStack adapter's recursive `stripUnserializable` pass over
every argument.

Centralizes outgoing form-state normalization in the shared
server-function hooks, before Next.js or TanStack Start serializes the
request. Callers can now pass their existing state directly. This moves
custom component and validator stripping and upload metadata conversion
to the shared request boundary, replacing ad hoc cleanup at individual
call sites.

Form state includes rendered React elements alongside its data. Next.js
Server Actions can carry these elements as temporary references through
Flight, but TanStack's Seroval request encoder cannot serialize them.
The server already has the component configuration, so those component
trees do not need to travel back.

Adds accessible names to admin list-view row-selection checkboxes.

1. `CheckboxInput` forced `aria-label=""` and fell back to
`aria-labelledby={name}`, but row-select checkboxes do not provide a
matching label target.
2. `SelectRow` did not pass a row-specific accessible name, so assistive
technology exposed unlabeled controls in the list view.

This change lets `CheckboxInput` accept explicit `aria-label` and
`aria-labelledby` props, generates localized row labels from
`useAsTitle` with an `id` fallback, and adds an e2e regression that
checks for `Select post1` and `Select post2`.

fix: connect to the correct Next.js dev HMR endpoint per version (#17632)

### What?

Payload's config hot reload in development stopped working on Next.js
16.3. Adding a collection or a field had no effect until the dev server
was restarted.

Next.js 16.3 renamed the dev HMR WebSocket endpoint:

- Old: `/_next/webpack-hmr` — [`router-server.ts#L859-L860` on
`v16.2.7`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/v16.2.7/packages/next/src/server/lib/router-server.ts#L859-L860)
- New: `/_next/hmr` — [`router-server.ts#L946-L947` on
`v16.3.0`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/v16.3.0/packages/next/src/server/lib/router-server.ts#L946-L947)

The client moved with it, in
[`client/dev/hot-reloader/app/web-socket.ts`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/v16.3.0/packages/next/src/client/dev/hot-reloader/app/web-socket.ts).
There is no alias in either direction: `/_next/webpack-hmr` does not
appear anywhere in the 16.3.0 build, and `/_next/hmr` does not appear
anywhere in 16.2.7.

request:
fix: dev HMR reload not working when Next.js basePath is set (#18484)

## Summary

With a Next.js `basePath` such as `/cms`, Payload did not reload config
changes in the dev server. A hard refresh also did not show the changes.
This PR makes Payload connect to the correct HMR WebSocket URL when
`basePath` is set. Config changes now show again in dev.

```
Next.js listens on:   ws://localhost:3000/cms/_next/hmr
Payload connected to: ws://localhost:3000/_next/hmr     ← no prefix, no reload messages
```

`PAYLOAD_HMR_URL_OVERRIDE` continues to work as before.
